stem: A company operates in the EU and the US. Regulation requires EU log data to stay in the EU. Which logging design do you recommend?

options.text: One Log Analytics workspace per geography (EU and US)
options.explanation: Correct: workspaces store data in their region.

options.text: One workspace in the US for everything
options.explanation: EU data would leave the EU.
Many workspaces without a residency reason add cost and complexity.

options.text: Send all logs to a storage account only

explanation: Data residency is a valid reason for more than one workspace.

stem: Firewall logs are huge, queried only during investigations, and must be kept 2 years at low cost. Alerts are not needed on them. What do you recommend?

options.text: Ingest them into a table using the Basic logs plan
options.explanation: Correct: cheaper ingestion for high-volume troubleshooting logs.
Most expensive option for rarely queried data.

explanation: Use table plans to match cost to how logs are used: Analytics for alerting and frequent queries, Basic/Auxiliary for high-volume, rarely queried logs.

stem: Each application team must see only logs from its own resources in a shared Log Analytics workspace. What do you use?

options.text: Resource-context access with Azure RBAC on the resources

options.explanation: Policy does not control log reading.

explanation: Resource-context RBAC returns only records from resources the user can access; table-level RBAC adds finer control.

stem: The security team uses a third-party SIEM that must receive Azure resource logs in near real time. How do you route them?

options.text: Diagnostic settings that stream to Event Hubs
Diagnostic settings to a storage account
Export from Log Analytics once a week

explanation: Event Hubs is the destination for streaming logs to external systems.

stem: Diagnostic settings must be configured on every new key vault in 30 subscriptions, automatically. What do you recommend?

options.text: An Azure Policy with the DeployIfNotExists effect assigned at a management group
A script run manually each month

options.explanation: DCRs are for agent-based collection, not resource logs.

explanation: Built-in 'enable logging by category group' policies deploy diagnostic settings at scale.

stem: Windows VMs must send only the System and Application event logs (Error and Warning) to a workspace. What do you configure?

options.text: Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection rule selecting those events
A diagnostic setting on the VM
options.explanation: Guest OS logs need the agent and a DCR.

explanation: Data collection rules define which guest data the Azure Monitor Agent collects and where it sends it.

stem: Users report a web app is slow. You need to see which database or API call takes the longest for each request. What do you recommend?
explanation: Application Insights records requests and dependency calls with timing.

stem: The SOC needs to correlate security events from Azure, Microsoft 365 and on-premises firewalls and run automated responses. What do you recommend?
explanation: Sentinel runs on a Log Analytics workspace with connectors, analytics rules and playbooks.

stem: Which TWO features help monitor AKS clusters?

options.text: Azure Monitor managed service for Prometheus
VM insights dependency map for each pod

explanation: Container insights plus managed Prometheus (and Grafana) are the AKS monitoring stack.

stem: You sync 10,000 users from AD. Sign-in must keep working if the on-premises datacenter is offline, and leaked passwords must be detected. Which method?

options.explanation: Users must keep their AD identity.

explanation: PHS has no on-premises dependency at sign-in and enables leaked-credential detection.

stem: Admins must use MFA, and access to the Azure portal from unmanaged devices must be blocked. What do you recommend?
explanation: Conditional Access combines user, app, device and location conditions.

stem: Users must sign in without passwords using phishing-resistant authentication on shared kiosk PCs. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Correct: phishing-resistant and not tied to one PC.
Weak and not a sign-in method.

explanation: FIDO2 keys and passkeys are phishing-resistant and portable.

stem: A consumer app needs sign-up and sign-in for millions of customers with email or Google accounts. What do you recommend?

options.text: Microsoft Entra External ID in an external tenant
B2B collaboration guests in the workforce tenant
Create member users for each customer

explanation: External ID is the customer identity solution (successor to Azure AD B2C).

stem: A GitHub Actions workflow deploys to Azure. Security forbids long-lived client secrets. What do you recommend?

options.text: Workload identity federation on an app registration or user-assigned managed identity
A client secret valid for 2 years

explanation: Federated credentials trust GitHub's OIDC token, so no secret is stored.

stem: Several web apps must use the same identity to access a database, and it must survive if one app is deleted. Which identity?

options.text: A system-assigned managed identity per app
options.explanation: Deleted with each app and not shared.

options.text: A shared SQL login in app settings

explanation: User-assigned identities are standalone resources that can be attached to many resources.

stem: Engineers should become Contributor on production only when needed, for at most 4 hours, with a justification. What do you recommend?

options.text: Permanent Contributor with an access review

explanation: PIM provides just-in-time, time-bound activation with justification and approval.

stem: Support staff must only start, stop and restart VMs in one resource group. No built-in role is that narrow. What do you do?

options.text: Create a custom role with those actions and assign it to their group at the resource group

explanation: Custom roles list exactly the allowed actions; assign to a group at the narrowest scope.

stem: In a shared container, users from each project may read only blobs tagged with their project. What do you recommend?

options.text: Storage Blob Data Reader with an ABAC condition on the blob index tag

options.explanation: Hard to manage and not identity-based.

explanation: ABAC conditions filter data access by attributes such as blob index tags.

stem: Remote employees need an on-premises intranet site with MFA. The network team will not open inbound firewall ports. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Correct: outbound connectors with Entra pre-authentication.

options.text: Publish the site on a public IP

options.explanation: A managed domain, not remote access.

explanation: Application proxy publishes on-premises web apps securely.

stem: A legacy app moved to Azure VMs requires LDAP and Kerberos. The company wants no domain controllers to patch. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Publishes web apps; does not provide LDAP.

explanation: Domain Services is a managed domain compatible with LDAP, Kerberos and NTLM.

stem: The company wants to replace its VPN so remote users reach private apps on various TCP ports, with Conditional Access per app. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Correct: Zero Trust network access per app.
The thing being replaced; network-wide access.

explanation: Private Access (Global Secure Access) gives per-app access to private resources on any port.

stem: Customer-managed keys must be protected by HSMs at the lowest cost, without dedicated hardware. Which service?
explanation: Premium adds HSM-protected keys to Key Vault.

stem: A web app must read a database password from Key Vault without storing any credential. What do you recommend?

options.text: Enable a managed identity on the app and grant it Key Vault Secrets User
Store the vault's access key in app settings
options.explanation: Key Vault has no shared access key; and that would be a secret.

options.text: Grant the app Owner on the vault

explanation: Managed identity + RBAC data role is the standard pattern.

stem: Which TWO settings help ensure keys used for customer-managed encryption cannot be permanently destroyed by a malicious admin?

options.explanation: Correct: deleted keys can be recovered.
Correct: prevents permanent deletion during retention.

explanation: Soft delete plus purge protection keep deleted keys recoverable for the retention period.

stem: All production subscriptions must allow only EU regions, and new production subscriptions must get the rule automatically. Where do you assign the policy?

options.text: On a management group that contains the production subscriptions
options.explanation: Correct: new subscriptions placed there inherit it.

options.text: On the tenant root group for all subscriptions

explanation: Policies assigned at a management group apply to all subscriptions under it, now and in future.

stem: Finance needs costs by cost center. Resource groups already have a CostCenter tag, but resources inside often don't. What do you recommend?

options.text: An 'Inherit a tag from the resource group' policy with Modify and a remediation task
A separate subscription per cost center
options.explanation: Heavy change for a reporting need.

explanation: Modify policies add or copy tags; remediation fixes existing resources.

stem: Which management group design follows Azure landing zone guidance?

options.text: Platform (Identity, Management, Connectivity), Landing zones (Corp, Online), Sandbox, Decommissioned
One management group per department, mirroring the org chart
options.explanation: Org charts change; design for policy.

options.text: Ten nested levels for fine control
No management groups; policy per subscription

explanation: The landing zone hierarchy groups subscriptions by the policies and access they need.

stem: Auditors need a report showing how Azure resources meet PCI DSS controls. What do you recommend?

options.text: The Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard with the PCI DSS standard

explanation: Defender for Cloud maps assessments to regulatory standards.

stem: A company used Azure Blueprints to deploy compliant subscriptions. Blueprints is deprecated. What do you recommend instead?

options.text: Template specs and deployment stacks with Azure Policy

explanation: Microsoft recommends template specs and deployment stacks (plus policy) to replace Blueprints.

stem: A Deny policy blocks a sandbox team that has an approved, temporary need for public IPs. Others must stay blocked. What do you recommend?

options.text: A policy exemption (Waiver) on the sandbox scope with an expiry date
Change the effect to Audit everywhere

explanation: Exemptions exclude a scope from an assignment, with a category and expiry.

stem: Every quarter, team owners must confirm that guest users still need access to their Microsoft Teams. Unconfirmed guests must lose access. What do you recommend?

options.text: Access reviews with auto-apply of results

explanation: Access reviews certify access and can remove denied users automatically.

stem: Contractors must request a bundle of groups and apps, get manager approval, and lose access automatically after 6 months. What do you recommend?
explanation: Access packages bundle resources with approval and expiration.

stem: When HR records an employee's last day, their account should be disabled and removed from groups automatically. What do you recommend?
explanation: Lifecycle workflows automate joiner, mover and leaver tasks from HR attributes.

stem: You migrate 40 SQL Server databases that use SQL Agent jobs, cross-database queries and Database Mail. You want PaaS with minimal changes. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: No SQL Agent or cross-database queries.
Works but is IaaS, not PaaS.

explanation: Managed Instance supports instance-scoped SQL Server features as PaaS.

stem: An application requires SQL Server Reporting Services on the same server and a third-party backup agent installed on the OS. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Correct: OS access and full feature set.

explanation: Only a VM gives OS-level control.

stem: A new cloud-native app needs one relational database with the least administration. What do you recommend?
explanation: SQL Database is the most managed relational option for new apps.

stem: A database is 45 TB and growing, and must scale compute quickly. Which tier?

options.explanation: Correct: up to 128 TB and fast scaling.

explanation: Hyperscale separates compute and storage for very large databases.

stem: A SaaS vendor has 250 small tenant databases. Each is busy at different times. Cost must be minimised. What do you recommend?
explanation: Elastic pools suit many databases with varying, non-overlapping usage.

stem: A test database is used for about 2 hours a day at unpredictable times. You want to pay as little as possible. What do you recommend?
explanation: Serverless bills per second of use and pauses when idle (General Purpose).

stem: Heavy reports slow down OLTP on a Business Critical database. You want to fix it without extra cost. What do you recommend?

options.text: Read scale-out with ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly for reports
options.explanation: Correct: Business Critical includes a readable replica.

options.text: Move reports to a separate database copy every night

explanation: Read scale-out uses the built-in readable replica at no extra cost.

stem: A multi-tenant app will outgrow any single database. Each tenant's data must stay together and be movable. What do you recommend?

options.text: Shard by tenant across databases using elastic database tools
Scale up to the largest Business Critical size

explanation: Horizontal sharding with a shard map spreads tenants across databases.

stem: Which tier lets you add up to 30 named replicas for independent read workloads?
explanation: Hyperscale supports named replicas for read scale-out.

stem: Database administrators must not be able to view social security numbers, but the app must use them. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Data is decrypted for anyone querying.
Privileged users see the real values.

explanation: Always Encrypted keeps plaintext out of the database engine.

stem: Each regional sales manager must see only orders from their region in the same table. What do you recommend?
explanation: RLS filters rows per user with security predicates.

stem: Which TWO features detect or record suspicious database activity?
explanation: Auditing records events; Defender for SQL detects threats such as SQL injection.

stem: An existing MongoDB application must move to a managed Azure service without changing its drivers. What do you recommend?
explanation: The MongoDB API keeps drivers and tools working.

stem: A Cosmos DB container uses /country as partition key. Writes are throttled because most users are in one country. What do you recommend?

options.text: Choose a high-cardinality partition key such as /userId (or a hierarchical key)

explanation: Partition keys should have many distinct values and spread requests evenly.

stem: Which consistency level is the Cosmos DB default and guarantees users read their own writes within a session?

options.explanation: Lag bounded by time or versions.

explanation: Session is the default and most widely used level.

stem: Data engineers need folders with POSIX-style ACLs and fast directory renames for Spark jobs. What do you recommend?

options.text: Blob Storage with a flat namespace

options.explanation: File shares, not an analytics lake.

explanation: Data Lake Storage adds a hierarchical namespace optimised for analytics.

stem: Windows file servers must be replaced with a managed SMB share that keeps NTFS-style permissions from AD. What do you recommend?
explanation: Azure Files offers SMB shares with AD DS or Entra Kerberos authentication.

stem: SAP HANA needs shared NFS storage with sub-millisecond latency and very high throughput. What do you recommend?
explanation: NetApp Files is certified for SAP HANA and high-performance workloads.

stem: Log files are read often for 2 weeks, rarely afterwards, and must be deleted after 1 year with no manual effort. What do you recommend?

options.text: A lifecycle management policy: Hot → Cool after 14 days, delete after 365 days
Keep everything in Hot and delete manually

options.explanation: Logs are read in the first 2 weeks.

explanation: Lifecycle rules automate tiering and deletion.

stem: An IoT app writes millions of small blobs per hour and needs consistently low latency. What do you recommend?

options.text: A Premium block blob storage account

explanation: Premium block blob uses SSDs for high transaction rates and low latency.

stem: Compliance archives must be kept 10 years, are almost never read, and can wait 15 hours for retrieval. The account must also use geo-redundancy. Which combination?

options.text: Archive tier on a GRS account
options.explanation: Correct: Archive supports LRS, GRS and RA-GRS.

options.text: Archive tier on a GZRS account
options.explanation: Archive is not supported on GZRS.
Costs more for data this cold.

explanation: Archive is the cheapest tier and requires LRS, GRS or RA-GRS.

stem: Financial records must be impossible to modify or delete for 7 years, even by administrators. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Protects the account, not blob data, and can be removed.

explanation: Locked time-based retention makes blobs WORM for the period.

stem: You need a copy of blob data that survives even if an attacker deletes the whole storage account. What do you recommend?

options.text: Vaulted backup for blobs in a Backup vault
options.explanation: Correct: the copy lives outside the account.
Lost if the account is deleted.

explanation: Vaulted backup stores data in a separate vault.

stem: Data must survive a zone failure and a full regional outage, and the secondary must be readable at all times. Which redundancy?

options.explanation: No zones in the primary and secondary not readable.

explanation: RA-GZRS = zones + secondary region + read access.

stem: Nightly copies from an on-premises SQL Server to Data Lake Storage must be orchestrated with retries and monitoring. The server has no public endpoint. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Data Factory with a self-hosted integration runtime

explanation: A self-hosted IR lets Data Factory reach private sources.

stem: Hundreds of existing SSIS packages must run in Azure with minimal changes. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure-SSIS integration runtime in Data Factory

explanation: The Azure-SSIS IR lifts and shifts SSIS packages.

stem: Factory machines send readings every second. An alert must fire within seconds when a 1-minute average exceeds a limit. What do you recommend?

options.text: Event Hubs with Azure Stream Analytics
Blob storage with a lifecycle rule

explanation: Stream Analytics computes windowed aggregates over live streams.

stem: Data scientists need notebooks and Apache Spark to build ML features on petabytes in a Delta Lake. What do you recommend?
explanation: Databricks is the Spark lakehouse platform for engineering and ML.

stem: A company wants one SaaS analytics platform covering data engineering, warehousing, real-time analytics and Power BI, with minimal infrastructure to manage. What do you recommend?

options.text: A set of VMs with open-source tools

explanation: Fabric unifies analytics workloads on OneLake as SaaS.

stem: Engineers must run ad-hoc KQL queries over billions of telemetry records with results in seconds. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Optimised for warehouse SQL, not KQL telemetry.
Not at that scale for log analytics.

explanation: Data Explorer is built for fast log and time-series analytics with KQL.

stem: An app's VMs must run in another region within a few hours of a regional outage, losing at most a few minutes of data. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Site Recovery replication to a secondary region
Daily Azure Backup with cross-region restore
options.explanation: RPO up to a day and slower recovery.
Don't protect against a regional outage.

explanation: Site Recovery provides minute-level RPO and orchestrated regional failover.

stem: A workload has an RPO of 24 hours and an RTO of 48 hours. What is the most cost-effective recovery design?

options.explanation: More cost than these targets need.

explanation: Relaxed targets are met by backup alone.

stem: Disaster recovery must be proven every quarter without affecting production. What do you recommend?

options.text: Site Recovery test failover into an isolated network
Planned failover of production every quarter
Restore a backup to the same VNet

explanation: Test failover creates VMs in an isolated network while replication continues.

stem: Ransomware encrypted a VM's disks this morning. You need it back as it was two days ago. What do you use?

options.text: Azure Backup restore from a recovery point

options.explanation: Replicas may contain the encrypted data.

explanation: Point-in-time backups recover from corruption and ransomware.

stem: Backups must survive even if an attacker with admin rights tries to delete them or shorten retention. What do you recommend?

options.text: Immutable vault plus soft delete and multi-user authorization (Resource Guard)
Daily backups to a second subscription without protection

explanation: Immutability, soft delete and MUA protect backups against malicious admins.

stem: File servers on-premises must back up selected folders to Azure without extra servers. What do you recommend?

options.text: The MARS agent with a Recovery Services vault

explanation: The MARS agent backs up files, folders and system state directly to Azure.

stem: A SQL database must fail over to another region with an RPO of seconds, and apps must not change connection strings. What do you recommend?

options.text: An auto-failover group with its listener endpoint

options.explanation: RPO about an hour and long RTO.

explanation: Failover groups replicate asynchronously and provide stable listener endpoints.

stem: Auditors require yearly backups of a SQL database kept for 7 years. What do you configure?

options.text: Long-term retention (LTR) with yearly backups for 7 years
Export a BACPAC manually each year

explanation: LTR keeps full backups up to 10 years.

stem: A developer deleted rows in a production Azure SQL database 30 minutes ago. What is the fastest supported recovery?

options.text: Point-in-time restore to a new database just before the deletion, then copy the rows back

options.explanation: The geo-secondary has the deletion too.

explanation: PITR restores to any point in the retention window as a new database.

stem: Users overwrite blobs by mistake and occasionally delete them. You need recovery for 30 days at low effort. What do you recommend?

options.text: Blob versioning plus soft delete (30 days)

explanation: Versioning recovers overwrites; soft delete recovers deletions.

stem: An Azure file share must be backed up daily with 30-day retention, and single files must be restorable by admins. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Correct: snapshot-based policy with item-level restore.

explanation: Azure Backup manages share snapshots (and vaulted copies) with retention and item-level restore.

stem: Blob data must be recoverable even if the storage account is deleted, with copies in another region. What do you recommend?

options.text: Vaulted backup for blobs in a geo-redundant Backup vault

explanation: Vaulted backup copies data to a Backup vault, which can be geo-redundant.

stem: A VM-based web tier must keep running if a datacenter in the region fails. The region has availability zones. What do you recommend?

options.text: A VM Scale Set across zones 1, 2 and 3 behind a zone-redundant Standard Load Balancer
Two VMs in the same zone

stem: An app must survive a full regional outage with near-zero downtime and serve users from the nearest region. What do you recommend?

options.text: Active-active deployments in two regions behind Azure Front Door

stem: An app needs a web tier (99.95%) and a database (99.99%) at the same time. What is its composite SLA?

options.explanation: Composite availability is lower, not higher.

explanation: Services needed together multiply their SLAs.

stem: An Azure SQL database must survive a zone outage with no data loss and without changing regions. What do you recommend?

options.text: Enable zone redundancy on the database

explanation: Zone-redundant configuration places synchronous replicas in different zones.

stem: SQL Server on Azure VMs must stay available during a zone failure with automatic failover. What do you recommend?

options.text: An Always On availability group with replicas in different zones

options.explanation: For PaaS, not SQL on VMs.

explanation: Availability groups replicate databases across VMs placed in different zones.

stem: A SQL Managed Instance must continue in another region after a regional outage, and reports should read from the secondary. What do you recommend?

options.text: A failover group for the managed instance
options.explanation: Correct: readable secondary and listener endpoints.

explanation: Managed Instance uses failover groups for geo-replication.

stem: A global app must accept writes in every region and stay writable during a regional outage. What do you recommend?

options.text: Cosmos DB with a single write region

explanation: Multi-region writes let every region accept writes.

stem: Images must remain readable during a regional outage without waiting for failover, and survive a zone failure. Which redundancy?
explanation: RA-GZRS combines zones with a readable secondary region.

stem: Which Cosmos DB setting automatically promotes a secondary region if the write region becomes unavailable?
explanation: Service-managed failover promotes a read region by the priority list.

stem: A team must host a Java web API with deployment slots, custom domains and autoscale, and wants minimal operations. Which compute?
explanation: App Service is the managed web platform with slots and domains.

stem: A workload must run on hardware not shared with any other customer for compliance, while keeping VM flexibility. What do you recommend?
explanation: Dedicated Host provides single-tenant physical servers for your VMs.

stem: Which question should you answer FIRST when choosing compute in the Azure compute decision tree?

options.text: Is it a lift-and-shift migration or a cloud-optimised/new app?

options.explanation: Only if you end up on VMs.

explanation: The decision tree branches first on migrate-as-is versus build or modernise.

stem: A 3D rendering job can be interrupted and restarted. Cost must be minimal. What do you recommend?
explanation: Spot uses spare capacity at deep discounts and can be evicted.

stem: A SQL Server VM will run 24/7 for three years. You hold Windows Server and SQL Server licences with Software Assurance. Which TWO reduce cost most?
explanation: Combine committed-use discounts with Hybrid Benefit for existing licences.

stem: Call-centre staff need a managed Windows desktop with company apps from home on personal devices. What do you recommend?

options.text: One VM per user with RDP from the internet

options.explanation: Admin access to VMs, not user desktops.

stem: Twelve microservices must scale on HTTP traffic and Service Bus queue length, including to zero. The team doesn't want to manage a cluster. What do you recommend?

stem: The platform team needs Kubernetes custom resource definitions, operators and a service mesh. What do you recommend?
explanation: AKS provides the full Kubernetes API.

stem: Container images must be stored once and pulled from registries in three regions over private endpoints. Which registry design?

options.text: Azure Container Registry Premium with geo-replication and private endpoints

stem: Every image uploaded to a container must be resized within seconds. Volume varies from zero to thousands per minute. What do you recommend?

options.text: An Azure Function triggered by Event Grid blob events on the Flex Consumption plan
A VM polling the container every minute
A Logic App Standard with a timer

stem: An order workflow must call three services in sequence, wait up to 5 days for a manager's approval, and resume. What do you recommend?

options.text: A single function with a sleep loop

stem: Business analysts must build a workflow that saves email attachments to SharePoint and creates a Salesforce record, with little code. What do you recommend?
explanation: Logic Apps provides managed connectors and a designer.

stem: A bank runs 20,000 independent risk simulations each night on hundreds of cores, and wants the lowest cost. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Slow and a single point of failure.
Not for long CPU-heavy jobs at this scale.

stem: A containerised data-cleanup task must run every night for 20 minutes without managing VM pools. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Batch with a dedicated pool

stem: Tightly coupled CFD simulations need low-latency interconnect between nodes and a fast parallel file system. What do you recommend?

options.text: HPC VM sizes with InfiniBand in a Batch or CycleCloud cluster, with Azure Managed Lustre

options.text: Service Bus queue with sessions, duplicate detection and dead-lettering

stem: One order message must reach billing, shipping and analytics, and each service only wants certain order types. What do you recommend?

options.text: A Service Bus topic with filtered subscriptions

stem: When should you choose Azure Queue Storage over Service Bus queues?

stem: Whenever a resource is created in any subscription, a function must check its tags within seconds. What do you recommend?

options.text: Event Grid system topic subscription for resource events
A timer function scanning every hour

options.explanation: Azure doesn't post resource events there.

stem: Two million devices send telemetry every few seconds; several analytics apps must read the same stream independently. What do you recommend?

stem: An existing Kafka-based producer must send to Azure without code changes, and data must also land in a data lake automatically. What do you recommend?

stem: Internal APIs must be published to partners with subscription keys, per-partner quotas, versioning and self-service documentation. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Layer 7 routing, no developer portal or products.

explanation: API Management provides products, policies, versions and a developer portal.

stem: APIs run in two on-premises datacenters and Azure. They must share one set of policies and a single control plane. What do you recommend?

options.text: API Management with self-hosted gateways on-premises

options.explanation: Publishes web apps, not API products.

stem: Partners must be limited to 1,000 calls per hour each without changing backend code. Where do you implement it?

options.text: A rate-limit/quota policy in API Management

stem: A product catalogue is read thousands of times per second but changes hourly. The database is overloaded. What do you recommend?

stem: A global site's images and scripts load slowly for users far from the origin region. What do you recommend?

stem: Several web servers must share user session state so any server can handle the next request. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure App Configuration with feature flags and dynamic refresh
Key Vault secrets for every setting

stem: Apps read settings from App Configuration. Database passwords must not be stored there. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Still secrets in the wrong store.

options.text: Use a separate App Configuration store for secrets
options.explanation: App Configuration isn't a secret store.

explanation: App Configuration references Key Vault so secrets stay in Key Vault.

stem: Dev, test and prod must read different values for the same keys from one App Configuration store. What do you use?
explanation: Labels let the same key hold different values per environment.

stem: A web app must be released with zero downtime and instant rollback. What do you recommend?

options.text: Deploy to a staging slot, warm up, then swap
Deploy to a new region each time

explanation: Slot swap avoids downtime and can be reversed.

stem: Every environment must be created identically from source control, and changes reviewed by pull request. What do you recommend?

options.text: Infrastructure as code (Bicep or Terraform) deployed by CI/CD pipelines
Portal deployments documented in a wiki
Exported templates edited by hand per environment

explanation: IaC in Git with pipelines gives repeatable, reviewed deployments.

stem: Developers need to create short-lived environments from approved templates without raising tickets, with cost limits. What do you recommend?

options.text: Manual requests to the platform team

explanation: Deployment Environments provides governed self-service from catalogs.

stem: Before migrating any workload, the company must deploy management groups, a hub network, identity and policies. Which CAF methodology covers this?
explanation: Ready prepares the landing zone before adoption.

stem: Leadership must agree on business outcomes and build a business case for moving to Azure. Which CAF methodology?
explanation: Strategy defines motivations, outcomes and the business case.

stem: A web app must move quickly now, but the team wants to use managed services with only small code changes. Which approach?

options.text: Replatform (for example to App Service and SQL Managed Instance)

explanation: Replatforming makes small changes to use PaaS.

stem: You must discover 400 VMware VMs without installing agents on them, collect performance data and get Azure size and cost recommendations. What do you use?

options.text: The Azure Migrate appliance with performance-based assessments

options.explanation: Only for resources already in Azure.

explanation: The appliance discovers agentlessly and feeds assessments.

stem: You must find which servers communicate with each other so they move in the same wave. What do you use?
explanation: Dependency analysis maps server-to-server connections.

stem: Before migrating, the business wants a comparison of on-premises costs versus Azure over 5 years. What do you use?

options.explanation: No on-premises comparison from discovery data.

explanation: The business case compares on-premises and Azure TCO using discovered data.

stem: 300 VMware VMs must move to Azure within 3 months with no code changes and a test before cutover. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Migrate agentless server migration (rehost) with test migrations

explanation: Azure Migrate replicates VMware VMs and supports test migration and cutover.

stem: A company wants to move its VMware environment to Azure while keeping vSphere tools and without converting VMs. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Migrate rehost to Azure VMs

explanation: Azure VMware Solution runs VMware natively on Azure.

stem: Several ASP.NET web apps on IIS should move to a managed platform with minimal code change. What do you recommend?

options.text: Replatform to Azure App Service using Azure Migrate web app migration
Rehost the IIS servers as VMs

explanation: Azure Migrate assesses and migrates web apps to App Service.

stem: A 2 TB production SQL Server database must move to SQL Managed Instance with no more than 15 minutes of downtime. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Database Migration Service online migration
Offline migration with backup and restore

explanation: Online migration syncs changes until a short cutover.

stem: Databases use cross-database queries, CLR and SQL Agent. They must move to PaaS. Which target and tool?

options.text: SQL Managed Instance, migrated with DMS or the Managed Instance link

options.explanation: Those features aren't supported in SQL Database.

options.text: SQL Server on VMs with Data Box

explanation: Managed Instance supports instance-level features; DMS or MI link migrate with low downtime.

stem: Which tool checks on-premises SQL Server databases for compatibility issues with Azure SQL targets before migration?
explanation: Azure Migrate's SQL assessment reports readiness and recommended targets.

stem: 600 TB of archives must move to Blob Storage. The office has a 200 Mbps link that is busy during the day. What do you recommend?
explanation: Data Box ships large volumes offline when bandwidth is limited.

stem: Branch offices must keep fast local access to shared files while the master copy moves to Azure. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Files with Azure File Sync caching on local servers

explanation: File Sync tiers files to Azure while keeping hot files local.

stem: 50 TB of SMB and NFS shares must move to Azure Files and Blob over a good network link, managed centrally from Azure. What do you recommend?

options.explanation: Unneeded when the network is good.

explanation: Storage Mover is the managed service for migrating file shares to Azure storage.

stem: VMs in a subnet must call a partner API that only accepts two known source IPs. The VMs have no public IPs. What do you recommend?

options.text: A NAT gateway with two static public IPs on the subnet

options.explanation: Not available on private subnets and IPs aren't fixed.

options.text: A public IP on every VM

explanation: NAT gateway gives predictable, scalable outbound IPs.

stem: A public web app in two regions needs WAF protection, global load balancing and caching. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Front Door Premium with WAF
Application Gateway in each region only
options.explanation: Regional, no global routing or caching.
DNS routing without WAF or caching.

explanation: Front Door combines global routing, caching and WAF.

stem: All outbound internet traffic from spoke VNets must be filtered by FQDN and logged centrally. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Firewall in the hub with a 0.0.0.0/0 route from each spoke

options.explanation: No FQDN filtering or central logging.

explanation: Route spoke egress through Azure Firewall for central filtering and logging.

stem: A datacenter needs 10 Gbps to Azure with predictable latency, and traffic must not cross the public internet. What do you recommend?
explanation: ExpressRoute provides private, high-bandwidth connectivity.

stem: The ExpressRoute circuit must have a lower-cost backup path if it fails. What do you recommend?

options.text: A site-to-site VPN configured as failover for ExpressRoute private peering

explanation: ExpressRoute and site-to-site VPN can coexist, with VPN as backup.

stem: Eighty branch offices, three regions and many VNets need any-to-any connectivity with minimal routing administration. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Virtual WAN with hubs in each region
Self-managed hub VNets with UDRs everywhere

explanation: Virtual WAN provides managed hubs with automatic any-to-any routing.

stem: Tightly coupled VMs exchange many small messages and need the lowest, most consistent latency between them. Which TWO do you recommend?
explanation: Co-location plus SR-IOV reduce latency and jitter.

stem: Two offices on different continents, both connected to Azure by ExpressRoute, must exchange data over Microsoft's backbone instead of the internet. What do you recommend?
explanation: Global Reach links ExpressRoute circuits so sites communicate via Microsoft's network.

stem: Users worldwide complain that static content on a single-region site is slow. What is the most effective improvement?

options.text: Serve static content through Azure Front Door caching
Increase the App Service plan size

explanation: Edge caching brings content close to users.

stem: Outbound HTTPS traffic must be decrypted and inspected for malware and intrusion attempts. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Firewall Premium with TLS inspection and IDPS

explanation: Firewall Premium adds TLS inspection and signature-based IDPS.

stem: A public website must be protected against OWASP top 10 attacks such as SQL injection. What do you recommend?

options.text: Web Application Firewall on Front Door or Application Gateway

explanation: WAF managed rule sets cover OWASP threats.

stem: Security requires that certain ports (for example RDP from the internet) are always denied across all VNets, even if a team adds an NSG allow rule. What do you recommend?

options.text: Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rules
options.explanation: Correct: evaluated before NSGs and can't be overridden by teams.

explanation: Security admin rules enforce organisation-wide guardrails before NSG rules.

stem: A TCP-based game service runs on VMs in one region and needs load balancing with health probes. What do you recommend?
explanation: Regional, non-HTTP traffic uses Load Balancer.

stem: In one region, requests to /api must go to one pool and /images to another, with TLS termination and WAF. What do you recommend?
explanation: Application Gateway provides regional layer 7 routing with WAF.

stem: A non-HTTP service runs in two regions. Clients must be sent to the primary region and fail over automatically to the secondary. What do you recommend?
explanation: Traffic Manager routes any protocol by DNS with priority failover.
